findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so the vendor roster object and any other data land without an enforced SSE-KMS/AES256 default at the bucket level.

Unlike the sibling buckets this one sets neither an explicit private ACL nor an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so it relies entirely on account-level defaults to stay private and can be exposed by a later public ACL or policy.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial exports are stored without an enforced KMS or AES256 default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block protects this bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a later public bucket policy or ACL from exposing ledger data.
The model artifacts bucket lacks server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored artifacts without enforced default encryption.
No public access block is defined, so the bucket is not guarded against subsequently applied public ACLs or bucket policies.
Operational runbooks, which commonly contain infrastructure detail and procedural secrets, are stored with no server-side encryption configuration.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or policies.

The audit log destination bucket has no public access block; it carries a log-delivery-write ACL and holds security-relevant records, so exposure via a later public ACL or policy would leak activity data.

The audit trail bucket enables versioning but configures no object lock or MFA delete, so audit evidence remains deletable by any principal with bucket write access, undermining the integrity of the log store other buckets depend on.
No bucket policy denies requests with aws:SecureTransport = false, so objects in this bucket (including the uploaded vendor roster) may be retrieved over cleartext HTTP.
No bucket policy denies non-HTTPS requests, permitting cleartext transmission of sensitive financial export data.

Access logs are written to aws_s3_bucket.audit_trail, which is created with force_destroy = true and no object lock; the logging dependency means log evidence for this bucket can be destroyed wholesale.
